signals.title: USD/NOK — G10 Bilateral Theme + Fed Repricing
signals.text: The G10 scorecard flags USD outperformance at +1.014% across 9 pairs against NOK underperformance at −2.021% across 2 pairs, establishing a 3.035% weekly spread. USD/NOK trades at 9.506, holding above its SMA20 at 9.354, SMA50 at 9.406, and SMA200 at 9.488 following a bullish engulfing daily bar. Macro momentum is reinforced by US CPI inflation re-accelerating, driving hawkish Fed repricing and pushing the US 2Y yield to 4.56%. While Norges Bank maintains a 4.50% policy rate vs the Fed at 4.00%, the 2Y yield spread shifted 17bp in the dollar's favor over the past 5 sessions. Retail sentiment data retail sentiment shows 91% long exposure, creating contrarian positioning friction against continued upside expansion. Trade bias: Long USD/NOK; upward momentum dominates while price holds above moving-average support. Catalyst: Norges Bank Financial Stability Report today at 08:30 UTC. Risk: A daily close below the SMA200 at 9.488 invalidates the bullish breakout structure.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Premium + Options Downside Hedging
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 158.87, remaining above its SMA20 at 157.95, SMA50 at 157.24, and SMA200 at 158.61 after clearing resistance at 158.47. A 265bp OIS carry advantage favors USD via SOFR at 3.88% against TONA at 1.23%, sustaining the structural upward drift. However, Saxo 1M 25d risk reversals print at −1.99, demonstrating severe put skew as institutional desks pay up for downside protection. The options market is aggressively hedging intervention risk as spot tests the 159.00 handle, with 160.00 marking the key historical threshold for Ministry of Finance action. CFTC positioning shows Leveraged Funds net short JPY by −21,213 contracts at the 92nd percentile of its 52-week range, leaving the carry trade vulnerable to sudden positioning squeezes. Trade bias: Bullish USD/JPY; positive carry supports the trend below official intervention thresholds. Catalyst: US Initial Jobless Claims at 13:30 UTC. Risk: Ministry of Finance FX intervention or verbal escalation triggers sharp downside liquidation below 157.95.

supports: technical regime points with the stated direction

signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded Speculative Short + Rate Divergence
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1157, positioned below its SMA20 at 1.1197, SMA50 at 1.1330, and SMA200 at 1.1542 in a consolidated box. CFTC data shows Leveraged Funds net short EUR by −104,030 contracts, sitting at the 2nd percentile of its 52-week distribution with a z-score of −1.80. The 144bp OIS carry advantage favors the dollar with SOFR at 3.88% against €STR at 2.44%, while the Fed policy rate at 4.00% maintains a 135bp spread over the ECB at 2.65%. Structural rates continue to favor the greenback, yet extreme institutional short positioning leaves the pair exposed to sharp short-covering on any European growth surprise. Desk models show BEER fair value at 1.1266 with a z-score of −2.19, indicating spot trades at a pronounced discount to fundamental equilibrium. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; persistent rate differentials cap rallies below moving averages. Catalyst: ECB President Lagarde speech today at 09:45 UTC. Risk: A daily close above the SMA20 at 1.1197 triggers positioning covering toward 1.1330.
evidence: EUR/USD BEER z-score: -2.19σ (spot 1.1157 vs fair value 1.1266)

signals.title: USD/CAD — Retail-Institutional Divergence + Technical Resistance
signals.text: USD/CAD trades at 1.4209, maintaining technical support above its SMA20 at 1.4060, SMA50 at 1.4054, and SMA200 at 1.3897. Retail sentiment data retail sentiment shows an extreme 85% short reading, which directly diverges from CFTC institutional positioning where Leveraged Funds are heavily net short CAD by −85,289 contracts. Spot advances entirely above its 20-day moving average following a wide-range expansion bar two sessions ago, testing multi-month highs. The pair benefits from a 136bp OIS carry premium favoring USD via SOFR at 3.88% against CORRA at 2.52%, alongside a 150bp policy rate spread. Retail crowd positioning is caught fighting the established institutional uptrend, raising the probability of a squeeze higher as retail stops trigger. Trade bias: Bullish USD/CAD; institutional trend and retail short imbalance support continuation. Catalyst: Canada Building Permits release at 13:30 UTC. Risk: A downside rejection below the 1.4100 handle weakens short-squeeze momentum.
